cards.title: Europe's AI power problem
cards.subtitle: Datacenter electricity
cards.quote: AI workloads grow +30% per year vs +9% for non-AI. AI servers rise from 21% of datacenter electricity to 44% by 2030. By 2035 (IEA lift-off scenario), datacenters reach ~4.4% of global electricity — a full Japan-sized grid.

cards.title: The grid is the bottleneck
cards.subtitle: Interconnection queue
cards.stat_sub: Median US grid interconnection queue (Gartner, Nov 2024)
cards.quote: Procuring GPUs takes months. Connecting to the grid takes 5+ years. Transformer and cable lead times doubled in three years. 40% of AI datacenters will be power-constrained by 2027. Clean power available NOW — not in 5 years — is a genuine moat.

cards.title: Inference eats the world
cards.subtitle: Workload shift
cards.stat_sub: Inference is now 280× cheaper per call. DeepSeek R1 trained −97% cheaper than GPT-4o. API traffic rose 10–40× in weeks.
cards.quote: As models get cheaper to train and serve, usage explodes. The efficiency → cost → adoption → demand loop means more infrastructure, not less. Inference siting — clean, cheap, and close to users — is the new strategic battleground.

cards.title: Memory bandwidth, not FLOPS
cards.subtitle: Hardware reality
cards.stat_sub: Share of H100 inference time spent waiting on HBM (Llama 3.1 70B)
cards.quote: Adding TFLOPS alone doesn't help. A 70B inference run on H100 is memory-bandwidth-limited 85% of the time. That's why inference silicon is fragmenting: Groq LPU for deterministic latency, MI300X for large-context (2.4× more HBM than H100), Blackwell CPX for 1T-param throughput.

cards.title: Where the margin lives
cards.subtitle: Value chain
cards.stat_sub: The primary revenue battleground is shifting from raw aggregation to inference-serving platforms.
cards.quote: Bare-metal GPU rental is a commodity. Orchestration (SUNK goodput 96%, Soperator open-source) narrows the moat. The durable advantage sits in L5 inference-serving platforms that capture sticky OpEx — where the operational knowledge of feeding real-time traffic compounds.

cards.title: H100 flood + B200 lock-in
cards.subtitle: Procurement timing
cards.stat_sub: CoreWeave's 2022–2023 H100 contracts expire 2025–26, releasing fleet into mid-market.
cards.quote: Procurement timing is a material cost lever. Buy B200 capacity today for frontier training; use the H100 flood for cost-effective inference PoCs. Interconnection + grid constraints mean the capacity you can connect to clean power matters more than the silicon on the shelf.
